messages.subject: multilevel SEM - specifying levels?
parts:
Hello,

I am conducting multilevel mediation analyses in lavaan, and had been using code passed down to me that didn't specify level blocks, and I didn't realize I needed to until reading through the conversations here (I don't know SEM, only stumbled upon the option to use MSEM with lavaan for multilevel mediation models!). 

My question is, does the code I am using still make sense given the multilevel nature of my data and my level-1 (within-person) focus?
My data = occasions nested within individuals; participants took 3 surveys across 10 days 
- 64 participants with at least 9 complete days of data each (i.e., complete = all 3 surveys completed that day)
- data is formatted such that N rows = N days for each participant, 1 day per row
- My main focus and RQs are at level 1 or within-persons, the only level 2 variables are between-persons control variables
- The level 2 controls are repeated down all of an individual's rows
- I have 1 predictor (X), 3 partial mediators (M1, M2, M3), and 1 outcome (Y)
- I have 5 control variables = four are level 2 (demographics = control1-control4), and one is level 1 (morning level of Y = AM.Ycontrol)

Below is the code I have been using:
model <-
"M1 ~ a1 * X + control1 + control2 + control3 + control4
M2 ~ a2 * X + control1 + control2 + control3 + control4
M3 ~ a3 * X + control1 + control2 + control3 + control4
Y ~ b1*M1 + b2*M2 + b3*M3 + c*Y + control1 + control2 + control3 + control4 + AM.Ycontrol
ind_eff1 := a1 * b1
ind_eff2 := a2 * b2
ind_eff3 := a3 * b3"
fit <- sem(model = modela, data = TDAT, se = "boot", bootstrap = 1000)
parameterEstimates(fita, boot.ci.type = "bca.simple", rsquare = TRUE, standardized = TRUE, zstat=TRUE, output = "pretty")

I also ran these regressions piecemeal using the mediate function in lme4 and get similar results across both methods. 
But based on what I've seen here, the code above wouldn't allow lavaan to automatically separate the within and between components of my level 1 variables. But would using the above code with group-mean (person-mean) mediators and DV, instead of the currently uncentered, effectively remove the between-person variance of level 1 variables (which I want) while still controlling for the level 2 control vars?

Or do I instead need to use the level-specifying block code?
If so, would this be the correct code to use?
model <- '
level: 1
#direct effects
Y ~ b1*M1 + b2*M2 + b3*M3 + c*Y + control1 + control2 + control3 + control4 + AM.Ycontrol

#mediator model
M1 ~ a1*X + control1 + control2 + control3 + control4 + AM.Ycontrol
M2 ~ a2*X + control1 + control2 + control3 + control4 + AM.Ycontrol
M3 ~ a3*X + control1 + control2 + control3 + control4 + AM.Ycontrol

#indirect effects
ind_eff1 := a1 * b1
ind_eff2 := a2 * b2
ind_eff3 := a3 * b3

level:2
#direct effects
Y ~ b1*M1 + b2*M2 + b3*M3 + c*Y + control1 + control2 + control3 + control4 + AM.Ycontrol

#mediator model
M1 ~ a1*X + control1 + control2 + control3 + control4 + AM.Ycontrol
M2 ~ a2*X + control1 + control2 + control3 + control4 + AM.Ycontrol
M3 ~ a3*X + control1 + control2 + control3 + control4 + AM.Ycontrol

#indirect effects
ind_eff1 := a1 * b1
ind_eff2 := a2 * b2
ind_eff3 := a3 * b3
'
fit.ML1 <- sem(model = MLmodel1,
                 data = TDATw1,
                 cluster = "ID", bootstrap = 1000)

Any help would be so appreciated.
Thanks very much in advance!!

Katie

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: multilevel SEM - specifying levels?
parts: does the code I am using still make sense given the multilevel nature of my data and my level-1 (within-person) focus?

I think it is unlikely that your Level-1 residuals are independent, given they are repeatedly measured on the same individual.  Autocorrelated Level-1 covariance structure is more plausible, but not possible in MLSEM with lavaan (or lme4 for that matter), but is available in nmle.  It is possible using wide-format data in lavaan (so it is a single-level SEM, using a (RI-)CLPM), but you might have trouble due to the small Level-2 sample size.
- I have 5 control variables = four are level 2 (demographics = control1-control4)
So those should only appear in the level: 2 model
one is level 1 (morning level of Y = AM.Ycontrol)

Are they the same for everyone?  If there is no Level-2 variance, or if you don't want a person-mean-centered interpretation of this predictor, then you can just specify them in the level: 1 model (in which case lavaan would not decompose that variable into latent Level-1 and -2 components).
the code above wouldn't allow lavaan to automatically separate the within and between components of my level 1 variables

Correct, not to mention your SEs and test statistics would not be robust to the violated independence assumption.  Unless you declared cluster = "ID" to request cluster-robust SEs and tests for your single-level model.  But then you wouldn't be able to answer research questions at Level 2.
Or do I instead need to use the level-specifying block code?

That tells lavaan to run a MLSEM.  Any variables declared in both models (i.e., at each level) will be decomposed in the "latent" way, which can be more robust when cluster means have a lot of sampling error.

https://psycnet.apa.org/doi/10.1037/a0012869

https://psycnet.apa.org/doi/10.1037/a0024376

But this means you need to use the uncentered variables in your MLSEM, so the decomposition happens implicitly during estimation.
If so, would this be the correct code to use?

No, remove the Level-2 predictors from the Level-1 model (maybe also vice versa; see my comment above about covariates).  
Also, use different parameter labels across levels, so you don't make the ecological/atomistic fallacy.  
If you are interested in estimating contextual effects, you can add user-defined (differences between) any analogous parameter across levels.
